avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May reduce methyldopa efficacy through enzyme induction and additive serotonergic effects; risk of hypertensive episodes
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; counsel patient on alternatives for mood support

avoid_supplements.name: Sympathomimetic amines (ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct antagonism of methyldopa's antihypertensive effect; risk of acute hypertensive crisis

avoid_supplements.name: Tyramine-containing supplements/herbals (high-dose ginseng, licorice root >3g daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potential hypertensive response due to catecholamine potentiation and COMT pathway interaction
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose formulations; monitor BP if low-dose use unavoidable

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate hypotensive effects; additive vasodilatory properties
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; counsel on potential additive effect; adjust BP monitoring frequency

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild additive antihypertensive effects; potential increased bleeding risk if used long-term
caution_supplements.action: Monitor BP and bleeding signs; generally safe but counsel on additive effects

caution_supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild independent antihypertensive activity
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; counsel patient to report significant BP changes

avoid_foods.name: High-tyramine foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented soy products, overripe bananas)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Tyramine can potentiate norepinephrine release and may reduce methyldopa efficacy or cause hypertensive episodes
avoid_foods.action: Educate patient on tyramine-restricted diet; focus on aged cheeses and cured meats as highest risk

avoid_foods.name: Licorice (food/candy >3g daily)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid activity leads to sodium retention and potassium loss; counteracts antihypertensive effect and increases hypokalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Advise avoidance of licorice-containing products; check electrolytes if chronic exposure occurred

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods (processed foods, salty snacks)
caution_foods.mechanism: Sodium excess counteracts antihypertensive efficacy and increases fluid retention
caution_foods.action: Reinforce sodium restriction guidelines (typically <2.3g daily); monitor BP control

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages (coffee, tea, energy drinks)
caution_foods.mechanism: May cause mild sympathomimetic stimulation and transient BP elevation
caution_foods.action: Counsel moderation; monitor BP response if consumption is high (>400mg daily)

monitoring_notes: Monitor blood pressure regularly and assess for orthostatic hypotension, especially with concurrent use of other antihypertensives. Baseline and periodic CBC/liver function recommended due to methyldopa's potential for autoimmune hemolytic anemia and hepatotoxicity; monitor for fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine.
